title: Assessment of protein inclusions in cultured cells using automated image analysis
protocol: Pre-warm 10 mL of serum-free culture medium per vial of cells to 37°C.
Remove cells from cryogenic storage and place the vial into a 37°C water bath.
Gently swirl the vial until there is a small particle of ice remaining.
Spray the vial with ethanol to sterilize it.
Transfer the contents to 10 mL of warm serum medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube at an appropriate g-force for 5 min to pellet your cells (e.g., 300 × g for NSC-34 cells, 150 × g for U-2 OS cells).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 μL of serum-supplemented culture medium.
Transfer resuspended cells into a culture flask containing appropriate volume of serum-supplemented culture medium.
Allow 2–3 passages of cells prior to performing experiments with them.
Pre-warm 500 mL of 1× PBS 0.5 mM EDTA to 37°C.
Pre-warm 50 mL of serum-free culture medium per T-75 flask of cells to 37°C.
Pre-warm 25 mL of Trypsin-EDTA dissociation solution to 37°C.
View cells under a microscope to determine confluency and health.
Discard growth medium from cultured cells.
Wash cells carefully twice with approximately 10 mL of 1× PBS 0.5 mM EDTA.
Wash cells once with approximately 10 mL of serum-free culture medium.
Add an appropriate volume of Trypsin-EDTA dissociation solution to the cells (e.g., 5 mL for a T-75 flask).
Incubate for 5 minutes.
Check cells under microscope to see if they have dissociated from the flask bottom.
Tap flask side lightly if cells are still adhered.
Pour the cell suspension into a sterile conical 50 mL tube.
Wash the stock vessel with approximately 10 mL of serum-free culture medium twice, pouring each wash into the tube containing the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at an appropriate g-force (e.g., 300 × g for NSC-34 cells or 150 × g for U-2 OS) for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and gently but thoroughly resuspend the cells into 1 mL of growth media.
Dilute the cells for hemocytometer counting (1 in 5 dilution).
Determine the volume of cell resuspension needed for plating based on user preferences.
Plate the cells into wells with relatively large surface areas, such as a well of a 6-well plate.
Place the plated cells into an incubator.
View plated cells under a microscope to ensure correct confluency and high viability (>90% viable cells).
Equilibrate approximately 10 mL Opti-MEM media to room temperature.
Defrost frozen plasmid stocks to room temperature.
Carry out transfection reagent protocol according to the manufacturer’s instructions using your predetermined optimized DNA:reagent ratio.
Add transfection mixture to cells and incubate for 24 h.
Re-plate the cells into multi-well plates after transfection incubation according to plating protocol.
Treat cells with drugs if necessary following transfection.
Pre-warm 4% PFA solution to 37°C.
Fix cells in warm PFA solution mixed with growth medium.
Avoid using cold PFA solution or neat (undiluted) warm PFA solution.
Utilize anti-fade solutions if image acquisition will result in long exposure times.
Add 1 volume of warmed 4% PFA solution per well of the plate containing transfected cells.
Incubate the cells for 15 min at room temperature, covered from light.
Aspirate the medium off the cells and discard appropriately as PFA is present.
Carefully add 1 volume of 4% PFA solution to each well in the plate and incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Add 0.1 M Tris (pH 8.0) to quench remaining PFA for 5 min.
Add 1 volume of 1× PBS 0.1% Triton X-100 to each well in the plate and incubate with gentle rocking for 5 min.
Wash the cells three times with 1× PBS for 5 min per wash.
Add 1 volume of Hoechst-33342 working solution to each well in the plate.
Incubate for 5 minutes with gentle rocking.
Wash the cells three times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes per wash.
Optional: Stain cell cytoplasm using ActinRed™ 555 ReadyProbes™ Reagent prior to nuclear counterstaining according to manufacturer’s directions.
Discard the 1× PBS and replace with 1 volume of antifade solution, if optional staining was performed.
Store the cells at 4°C protected from light until imaging.
Establish best practices for fluorescence microscopy in plate-based formats manually or using microscope controlling software with automatic focusing and acquisition.
Consult your microscope technician if you need help setting up your specific microscope.
Perform this step using an epi-fluorescent wide-field microscope, or alternatively a laser scanning or spinning disk confocal microscope.
Ensure the outcome is a set of high-quality fluorescence microscopy images for image analysis.
Check manually that the images are in focus and free from artefacts.
Verify that the images have fluorescence channels with adequate brightness.
Automatically determine poor quality images if desired, using defined methods.
Iterate acquisition and analysis settings to find optimal parameters for quantitative image analysis.
Turn on the microscope.
Turn on the light source.
Turn on the camera.
Place samples to be imaged in the same room as the microscope.
Allow samples to equilibrate to the same temperature as the microscope for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Set the light source emission power to the lowest setting.
Ensure the camera is set to acquire images in the highest bit-depth available, typically 16-bit.
Place the sample onto the stage.
Move the stage so that you are imaging in the sample well with the highest expected brightness of your FP-tagged protein of interest (POI).
Find the plane where the cells are in-focus using brightfield or another transmitted light imaging method.
If necessary, focus on the cells using the nuclear marker Hoechst-33342.
Turn up the light source emission for the chosen marker if needed.
View the cells in each channel necessary to excite the fluorophores present in the sample.
Check that no channel has signal exceeding the detection limits of the camera.
Decrease exposure time or illumination intensity for channels with overexposed pixels if detected.
Increase excitation power, exposure time, or binning for channels with insufficient signal, considering potential photobleaching and resolution limitations.
Move around to different locations in this well of the sample to ensure as few cells have saturated pixels.
Optimize excitation and acquisition settings so that the camera detects approximately 60% brightness if a large set of samples makes pixel optimization impractical.
Ensure that at least one well of each plate is a brightest sample control (e.g., an EGFP only control).
Switch between acquisition channels to ensure focus offsets are applied appropriately for wavelength effects on focal plane.
Set up the microscope acquisition software to automatically image more than 50% of the well area in multi-well plates using optimized settings.
Set up the autofocusing method that the microscope uses.
Ensure that you are autofocusing using the brightest channel, typically the nuclear marker for software-based methods.
Make sure your autofocus method searches a large enough distance in the axial plane to capture each well if plastic-bottomed plates are used.
Image your samples.
Save your data with a comprehensive file naming strategy.
Include date, plate ID, well, region, and channel information in file names for multi-plate experiments.
Manually investigate images for artifacts post acquisition.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl to reconstitute human recombinant leptin.
Manually check each image for aberrant features such as particulate matter, incorrect acquisition, or out-of-focus images.
Record the reason for removing an image from analysis if it contains grossly aberrant features.
Reimage areas with fewer than 300 detected cells at new locations free of artifacts.
Maintain image bit-depth across steps in the protocol for 16-bit images.
Ensure large image datasets contain information about the sample in each image.
Check with your technician regarding batch export options from commercial microscopy software.
Make a copy of your images for processing and analysis.
Open CellProfiler.
Drag and drop the folder(s) containing your copied exported images into the CellProfiler UI.
Establish the channel identifiers under the NamesAndTypes module.
Assign a name to “Images matching rules”.
Set up image groups under the Groups module in CellProfiler for individual plate and channel processing.
Right-click in the empty space below the Groups module in the main CellProfiler window and select “Image Processing > CorrectIlluminationCalculate”.
Select input images in the CorrectIlluminationCalculate module.
Choose between "Regular" or "Background" calculation for illumination functions.
Understand the source of uneven illumination in images.
Determine if images contain very few or many bright objects.
Calculate background for images with few bright objects.
Perform regular calculation for images with many bright objects.
Set Dilate objects option to No.
Select Rescale illumination function as Yes.
Choose Individual calculation or all as All First Cycle.
Select Smoothing Filter as Gaussian.
Choose a filter size large enough that little to no texture is apparent in the final illumination function.
For background calculation, set Block size appropriately.
Do not rescale illumination function for background calculation.
Choose Individual calculation or all as All First Cycle for background calculation.
Set Smoothing Filter as Gaussian.
Right-click in the empty space below the Groups module in the main CellProfiler window.
Go to "File Processing > SaveImages".
In the SaveImages module, maintain original image bit-depth.
Save the image from the first cycle.
Select the type of image to save as Image.
Choose From image filename for constructing file names.
Use the name of your image defined earlier in the NamesAndTypes module as the file prefix.
Output file location can be anywhere but typically within a subfolder housing images to be analyzed.
Right-click in the empty space below the Groups module in the main CellProfiler window.
Go to "Image Processing > CorrectIlluminationApply".
Input images will be those intended for correction.
Set illumination function from the CorrectIlluminationCalculate module.
Subtract the illumination function if you generated a background function.
Divide if you generated a regular illumination function.
Create a SaveImages module for each channel being illumination corrected.
Save the illumination-corrected images to a folder for later use.
Import a small subset of illumination-corrected nuclear channel images into ImageJ.
Activate the StarDist plugin.
Optimize StarDist parameters for best detection.
Run StarDist.
Open the new image and the ImageJ ROI-manager.
Go to “Show All” in the ImageJ ROI-manager.
Assess the accuracy of the StarDist plugin by looking for cases where it did not identify nuclei or it combined two nuclei into one nucleus.
Adjust parameters to enhance accuracy if necessary.
Determine appropriate settings for accurate identification of nuclei using StarDist.
Download the StarDist-BATCH ImageJ macro from ‘https://github.com/ljr979/Stardist-BATCH’ or ‘https://github.com/PlotkinLab/Stardist-BATCH’ and unzip the file to find the python file.
Drag and drop the python file onto your ImageJ main bar to open it.
Set language to python using the ‘Language’ option at the top of the new window.
Alter the parameters in lines 9–11 of the macro code to match those determined previously.
Replace `input_folder` with your directory path using forward slashes, e.g., `'C:/Data/Images/Experiment01/TileScan/'`.
Set `file_identifier` to specify the nuclear channel identifier, for example, `'DAPI'`.
Press the ‘Run’ button to execute the macro once inputs are correctly set.
The output will be new images named with a prefix of 'label_' followed by their original names.
Generate illumination corrected images for each channel of analysis.
Obtain StarDist identified nuclei images.
Segment cells into nuclear and cytoplasmic compartments using CellProfiler pipeline.
Generate feature measurements for classification of cells.
Create excel spreadsheets with individual cell measurements.
Generate files necessary for input into CellProfiler Analyst.
Load illumination corrected images into CellProfiler.
Setup the Metadata module for your image set.
Capture Plate number, well number, and sample identifier (e.g., mutant/drug).
Set up NamesAndTypes module to differentiate nuclear channel, aggregating protein channel, and StarDist images.
Add a ConvertImageToObjects module to the pipeline.
Input image = StarDist image.
Convert to Boolean image = No.
Add a MeasureObjectSizeShape module followed by a FilterObjects module.
Input objects = nuclei.
Filtering Mode = measurements.
Filtering Method = Limits.
Category = AreaShape.
Measurement = Area.
Filter using a minimum value.
Empirically determine the value that removes micronuclei without removing actual nuclei in experiments.
Shrink the nuclei by at least one pixel using an ExpandOrShrinkObjects module.
Determine the most appropriate number of pixels for shrinking to prevent the subsequent masking step from not removing untransfected cells.
Add an EnhanceOrSuppressFeatures module to the pipeline.
Subtract unwanted background from the cells using EnhanceOrSuppressFeatures.
Enhance speckles with an empirically determined feature size slightly above the size of entire cells.
Smooth the image enough that there are no jagged edges on cells using a Gaussian filter method.
Apply 4 or 2 pixels smooths to the image.
Add a Threshold module to the pipeline.
Create a binary image for overlaying onto identified nuclei using Global threshold strategy and Minimum Cross-Entropy threshold method with Log transform enabled.
Add a MaskObjects module to the pipeline.
Mask objects based on shrunken nuclei from step 24 to identify truly transfected nuclei and enhance subsequent cytoplasm identification.
Add an IdentifySecondaryObjects module to the pipeline.
Identify cell cytoplasm for each nuclei using propagation method in IdentifySecondaryObjects module.
Input image = image from EnhanceOrSuppressFeatures (step 25).
Input objects = objects from MaskObjects.
Threshold Strategy = Global.
Thresholding method = Minimum Cross-Entropy.
Log transform = yes.
Discard secondary objects touching image border = yes.
Load the properties file created from your CellProfiler pipeline into CellProfiler Analyst.
Open the Classifier module.
Fetch 50–100 random cells from the experiment.
Turn off the overlays of nuclear stains and StarDist.
Click on the menu for each channel and turn them off except for your channel of interest.
Sort cells by dragging and dropping from your requested set into classes based on whether they contain inclusions or not.
Add more classes if needed by clicking the button in the bottom right corner.
Sort approximately 20 cells into each class.
Fetch more cells if you run out of a certain phenotype.
Train using a classifier of your choice, such as random forest classification for accuracy or fast gentle boosting if training set size and quality are adequate.
Click on “train” in the window to train the classifier.
Wait for the classifier to calculate.
Request a number of cells from your inclusions class and sort them into their respective bins.
Request a number of cells from your no inclusions class and sort them into their respective bins.
Train the classifier again as necessary.
